text:
San Jose trailed by two goals with 12 minutes left, and Will Smith got them back in it. The 2023 fourth overall pick, drafted out of the U.S. National Team Development Program and a 71-point freshman at Boston College, scored on a power play at 8:00 of the third. He added a second at 10:39. Eleven seconds later Mason Marchment, who was never drafted and worked his way up as a free agent, scored on a 3% chance to make it 3-2 SJS. Three goals in under three minutes turned a game the Sharks had been losing all night.

Our numbers say the Canucks played the better game. Vancouver's 63% "deserved to win" figure (the share of simulated replays of every shot that the team wins) came from owning the first period, when VAN out-chanced SJS 1.62 to 0.80 in expected goals, which measures the quality of chances. Drew O'Connor and Liam Ohgren scored in the first two periods, though Ohgren's goal was a 5% look. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 23 of 25 shots and saved about one goal more than the chances against him deserved, including Paul Cotter's 30% look in the second. Leevi Merilainen allowed three on 24 shots, 0.71 goals worse than expected.

San Jose now has a comeback from two goals down to its name, and Smith, Marchment and Macklin Celebrini all had a hand in it. Vancouver outplayed the Sharks for most of two periods and went 0 for 3 on the power play, so it leaves with nothing to show for that. We'd watch whether the Canucks can turn that kind of control into a lead they hold.
